title: The Loose Drop
premise: Financial-crimes investigator Beatrix Sterling has spent two years in witness protection after testifying against the Voss syndicate, haunted by the night her handler died covering her escape. When she finds the safe house listed online with interior photos, she realizes someone inside the program is selling her location. To survive, Beatrix must decide whether to hand over the encrypted ledger — the one secret worth killing for — to the syndicate's fixer, or trust a disgraced former lover turned federal marshal to get her to the dawn extraction flight. She trades the ledger, but only after copying it: the flight leaves with her aboard, the syndicate's proof of corruption inside the Marshal Service exposed, and her past finally paid for.
about_author: Quentin Blackwood is the pen name of a former compliance officer who spent a decade tracing dirty money through offshore shells before turning to fiction. He writes thrillers from a coastal town he refuses to name, claiming anonymity is 'a professional habit.'

chapters.title: The Listing
chapters.summary: POV: Beatrix. Insomniac Beatrix scrolls real estate sites at 3 a.m. and finds her safe house listed, complete with photos of her own handwriting on the kitchen whiteboard. Her calls to the protection detail go unanswered. The emotional beat is cold dread — the realization that invisibility was an illusion someone sold while she slept beside it.

chapters.title: Clean Money
chapters.summary: POV: Beatrix, with an interlude from the fixer, Marek. A staged gas-leak inspection forces Beatrix out; she recognizes the inspector's shoes as syndicate-issue. Meanwhile Marek, the Voss fixer, reveals he bought the listing data from someone wearing a federal badge. The beat is paranoia tightening into certainty: the leak is inside the Marshals, and her handler's death wasn't random.

chapters.title: The Ledger
chapters.summary: POV: alternating Beatrix and Marshal Elias Kane, her ex-lover sent to extract her. Elias admits his own agency is compromised and offers a plan that requires the encrypted ledger as leverage against the corrupt deputy director. Beatrix must weigh duty, love rekindled under fire, and whether trusting him repeats the mistake that got her handler killed. Beat: love against duty at gunpoint.

chapters.title: Dawn Flight
chapters.summary: POV: Beatrix. At the airfield, Marek offers the trade; Beatrix hands over a decoy drive while Elias arrests the deputy director using her copied ledger as evidence. Marek escapes, but the syndicate's shield is gone. As the plane lifts off at sunrise, Beatrix sleeps for the first time since the incident. Beat: costly resolution — survival purchased with the secret itself.
